chunks: Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Is'haq ibn 'Ammar, from Abu Baseer, who said:

I asked him (peace be upon him) about locusts entering the provisions of people, so they tread on them without deliberately intending to kill them, or they pass by them on the road and step on them. He (peace be upon him) said: 'If you find a way to avoid them, avoid them; but if you kill them without deliberation, there is no problem.'
ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to kill locusts accidentally while protecting food or walking?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies the permissibility of accidental harm to locusts, emphasizing that unintentional killing is valid (la ba'sa) while encouraging avoidance (i'dal) if feasible. It reflects the Shia juristic principle of distinguishing between deliberate intent (ta'ammud) and natural occurrence in determining ritual purity and permissibility, particularly relevant for those in Ihraam. The ruling underscores the leniency in Islamic law regarding minor creatures when their destruction is not purposeful.
